_note: Deterministic phrase list for fair_housing.py. Categories follow the Fair Housing Act protected classes plus common state/local additions, steering proxies and MLS remark rules. This list catches known problem phrases; it is not legal advice and cannot catch every problem, so the skill also does a context review. Add your state's protected classes and your MLS's rules as new entries.

levels.NOTE: Style or terminology; does not affect PASS

entries.why: Describes who should live here (families/children). Advertising a preference based on familial status violates 42 USC 3604(c).
entries.rewrite: Describe the space instead: "four bedrooms and a flexible bonus room".

entries.why: Signals a preference for households with children.
entries.rewrite: Name the feature: "fenced backyard", "cul-de-sac lot".

entries.why: Signals a preference for households with children.
entries.rewrite: Name the feature: "large fenced yard", "bonus room upstairs".

entries.category: describes the buyer (familial / age / state classes)
entries.why: Describes who should live here instead of the property. Some groups are protected in some states (age, student status in a few cities).
entries.rewrite: Describe the feature that appeals: "home office with built-ins", "low-maintenance yard".

entries.why: Characterises residents by familial status.
entries.rewrite: Describe the property or amenities, not the residents.

entries.why: Excludes households with children (only HOPA-qualified 55+/62+ housing may restrict).
entries.rewrite: Remove. If the community is HOPA-qualified senior housing, say so factually and confirm with the broker.

entries.why: Describes the ideal occupant by marital or family status.
entries.rewrite: Describe size and layout: "easy-care two-bedroom plan".

entries.why: Describes the ideal occupant by family stage and age.
entries.rewrite: "Primary suite on the main level", "low-maintenance yard".

entries.why: Implies a household with a baby. Usually low risk, but describes people rather than space.
entries.rewrite: "Bedroom" or "flex room".

entries.why: Implies who will live there; widely used but many brokerages now avoid it.
entries.rewrite: "Guest suite", "secondary suite", "multi-generational floor plan" (describes the plan, not the people).

entries.why: Religious word. Fine inside a proper name used only as a location ("Christian Brothers Automotive"); not fine describing the property, area or buyer.
entries.rewrite: Remove unless it is part of a business or place name used only for directions.

entries.why: A house of worship as a selling point can signal religious preference. A widely known landmark used only for directions is lower risk.
entries.rewrite: Remove, or use a neutral landmark: "near the town square".

entries.why: Describes the area, home or residents by religion.
entries.rewrite: Remove. Describe the property only.

entries.why: Saint names usually point to a church or parochial school.
entries.rewrite: Remove, or replace with a neutral landmark or the street name.

entries.why: Religious-practice reference.
entries.rewrite: Describe the feature: "two dishwashers", "double ovens".

entries.why: Describes residents or buyers by race, color or national origin.
entries.rewrite: Remove. Describe the property only.

entries.why: Racial composition of an area.
entries.rewrite: Remove.

entries.why: Comments on who lives in the area.
entries.rewrite: Remove, or name concrete amenities.

entries.why: National-origin preference.
entries.rewrite: Remove.

entries.why: Racially coded description of an area.
entries.rewrite: Remove.

entries.why: "Exclusive" and "restricted" were historic codes for racial exclusion.
entries.rewrite: "Gated community" (if true), "limited homesites".

entries.why: Sex-based preference.
entries.rewrite: Remove; describe the space.

entries.why: Gendered description. Common, but describes the occupant.
entries.rewrite: "Bonus room", "media room", "studio", "hobby farm".

entries.why: Excludes or discourages people with disabilities.
entries.rewrite: Remove. Describe the feature: "three-story townhome", "second-floor unit, no elevator".

entries.why: Dated term for people; describing accessibility features is fine.
entries.rewrite: "Accessible", "wheelchair-accessible entry", "roll-in shower".

entries.why: Age preference is allowed only in HOPA-qualified 55+/62+ housing.
entries.rewrite: Keep only if the user confirms the community is HOPA-qualified; otherwise "single-level living".

entries.why: Describes the desired buyer's age.
entries.rewrite: Remove; describe the property.

entries.why: Source-of-income discrimination is illegal in many states and cities, and "no Section 8" is also used as a racial proxy.
entries.rewrite: Remove.

entries.why: Mentions housing assistance; check context.
entries.rewrite: Remove unless legally required wording.

entries.why: Describes residents or buyers by sexual orientation or gender identity.
entries.rewrite: Remove.

entries.why: Military status is protected in several states.
entries.rewrite: Remove.

entries.why: Safety and crime characterisations are a recognised steering proxy and cannot be verified by the agent.
entries.rewrite: Remove. Point buyers to official sources (local police department data) to evaluate themselves.

entries.why: Crime statements about an area can steer.
entries.rewrite: Remove; let buyers consult official sources.

entries.why: School-quality claims are a steering proxy and change over time.
entries.rewrite: State the assigned district factually: "Zoned to Cedar Hollow ISD (buyer to verify)".

entries.why: Subjective judgment about a neighbourhood can steer.
entries.rewrite: Name concrete, verifiable features: "sidewalks", "0.4 mi to the community pool".

entries.why: Characterises the people who live in the area, a classic steering signal.
entries.rewrite: Remove. Describe the property and verifiable amenities.

entries.why: Not a Fair Housing violation, but many MLSs and brokerages now prefer "primary".
entries.rewrite: "Primary bedroom", "primary suite".

entries.why: Under the 2024 industry settlement rules still in force, offers of buyer-broker compensation may not appear in MLS fields or remarks.
entries.rewrite: Remove from remarks. Compensation is discussed off-MLS under written agreements.

entries.category: MLS rule: contact info in public remarks
entries.why: Most MLSs prohibit phone numbers, emails and links in public remarks.
entries.rewrite: Move contact details to the agent fields or the flyer.

entries.category: MLS rule: showing instructions in public remarks
entries.why: Showing instructions, access codes and lockbox details belong in the private/agent remarks or showing fields, not public remarks.
entries.rewrite: Move to the agent-only remarks or showing-instructions field.
